quarterly_data.signal: The 10-Q states that in fiscal year 2026 demand from AI and cloud customers has continued to increase and is outpacing Lumentum's current supply, which has required it to make decisions on supply allocation; Lumentum is investing in manufacturing capacity both internally and with contract manufacturers. Capital expenditures were $284.5 million in the nine months ended March 28, 2026 (vs $177.1 million in the nine months ended March 29, 2025), and purchase obligations - legally binding commitments to purchase inventory and other commitments made in the normal course of business to meet operational requirements - were $1,795.6 million as of March 28, 2026 ($1,629.9 million due in less than 1 year).
quarterly_data.figure: capex $284.5 million (nine months ended March 28, 2026) vs $177.1 million; purchase obligations $1,795.6 million as of March 28, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Lumentum's net inventory purchases were concentrated with one contract manufacturer (not named), which accounted for 19% of total net inventory purchases in both the three and nine months ended March 28, 2026, versus 27% in both the three and nine months ended March 29, 2025; its contract manufacturers are located primarily in Thailand, Taiwan and Malaysia.
quarterly_data.figure: one contract manufacturer 19% of net inventory purchases (three and nine months ended March 28, 2026) vs 27%

quarterly_data.signal: On March 17, 2026 Lumentum acquired a manufacturing facility in Greensboro, North Carolina from a third party (not named), including land and building, machinery and equipment and an assembled workforce. As part of the transaction it entered into a transitional supply agreement under which Lumentum will manufacture wafers for that third party for approximately 15 months, acting as an agent (revenue recognized on a net basis).
quarterly_data.figure: transitional wafer supply agreement for approximately 15 months at the Greensboro, NC facility
